newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICA HAMMER 278 FOR EIGHT.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICA HAMMER 278 FOR EIGHT.

text.p: South Africa, unbeaten in their home triangular series, put the Indian attack to the sword with a challenging 278 for eight in the re-played one-day final at Kingsmead on Thursday.
Daryll Cullinan top-scored with a fluent 60 off 51 balls as the home side threatened a total in excess of 300 with six overs - and the threat of rain - remaining.
But Indian seamer Venkatesh Prasad took two wickets in as many balls in the 44th over to arrest South Africa's batting momentum on his way to final figures of 2-43.

After South African captain Hansie Cronje won his first toss of the tournament, the home side took full advantage of the batsman-friendly pitch as their entire top and middle order got among the runs.
Openers Gary Kirsten (51) and Andrew Hudson (19) built a solid foundation with a confident stand of 44 in 11 overs under leaden skies.
Although Hudson was then given out caught behind off fast bowler Javagal Srinath, Kirsten and Jacques Kallis (49) upped the tempo with a second-wicket partnership of 86 runs in 92 balls.
Kirsten, having reached his fourth 50 of the triangular series from 65 deliveries, was caught in the deep attempting a pull-sweep off all-rounder Robin Singh.

Kallis departed for 49 the very next ball - leg before wicket as he drove at Singh - but Cullinan and Jonty Rhodes (41) then took the innings to new heights as they pushed the run-rate to 5.9 per over with an electrifying stand of 91 in just 81 balls.
